role: WS-2 Ledger cell-state THRASH forensics (systems-architect, read-only)
summary: CONFIRMED the WS-1 "coverage thrash" mechanism empirically — but reframed by the data into TWO coupled pathologies, not one. (1) RECLAIM THRASH: cells cycle untested->testing(claim,attempts++)->lease-expire->reclaim->testing without terminalizing. The DB `ledger_cell.attempts` counter (each claim_cells does attempts+=1) proves it: applicable cells claimed >=2x = 622/2719 (23%) on prior scan 68a58881, 727/2122 (34%) on infinity 1f5fe7c8, and 428/2916 (15%, still climbing at only max=3 attempts 7h in) on the LIVE scan 84aea81a. Reclaim is PARTLY productive (blackboard handoff works: of >=2-attempt cells, ~51-64% eventually close tested_clean) but 35-48% die without a real result. LIVE smoking gun: 1654/1703 (97%) of currently-`testing` cells sit in expired-lease limbo (claimed_by set, lease_expires_at < now()) = exactly the re-claimable state, yet their last_progress is <5min because a periodic resolve pass (LIVE_CONVERGENCE, SYNC_INTERVAL_S=120) bumps last_progress independent of the lease — so the last_progress-based stuck-detector (STUCK_WINDOW_S=1200) never fires while the lease-based claim gate keeps re-handing them. Two clocks disagree. (2) STARVATION (the dominant terminal outcome, the flip side): while capacity concentrates on re-claiming the same ~600-720 cells, a comparable/larger set is NEVER claimed once (attempts=0) and gets swept to terminal `attempted` by finalize.py's retire-unreached sweep — 1054/2719 (39%) on 68a58881, 470/2122 (22%) on infinity. The `attempted` bucket therefore conflates cap-exhaustion (minor: the cap of 6 is rarely hit) with unreached-starvation (dominant: 81% and 55% of `attempted` cells have attempts=0). SELF-REPORT corroboration: ledger_updates.jsonl (agent coverage self-reports; no timestamp/worker/cell_id -> ordinal analysis) is 42.5%/36.9% redundant re-writes and 88.3%/91.3% of self-reported cells never get a terminal coverage line (endless "testing", up to 31 re-writes on one cell). NOTE ledger_updates.jsonl does NOT record claim/reclaim/worker transitions at all — it is the agent's self-graded coverage churn; the authoritative reclaim record is the DB attempts column.

Reclaim path 2 (fallback, dead worker): reclaim_expired_leases nulls claimed_by+lease for open cells past lease; absorb to 'attempted' only when attempts>=cap. [CODE] ledger/service.py:1543-1570.

questions.answer: Widely. DB attempts>=2 (applicable): 68a58881 622/2719=23%, 1f5fe7c8 727/2122=34%, LIVE 84aea81a 428/2916=15% and climbing (7h in, max attempts only 3). hypotheses.id: WS1-coverage-thrash: cells cycle claim/reclaim without terminalizing, stalling coverage
hypotheses.note: Reclaim thrash is real and measured (23-34% of applicable cells claimed >=2x; 97% of live testing cells in re-claimable limbo). BUT the dominant coverage-stall driver in FINALIZED scans is the coupled STARVATION: 39%/22% of applicable cells are never claimed once and are swept to 'attempted' unreached at finalize. Capacity concentrates on re-working a subset while another subset is never reached. The attempt-cap (6) is rarely hit, so cap-absorption is a minor contributor.

hypotheses.id: attempt-cap absorbs thrashed cells to 'attempted' during the run
hypotheses.note: Cap absorption requires attempts>=cap(6); only ~1-2 cells reached 6 on 68a58881 and ~152 on 1f5fe7c8. 81%/55% of 'attempted' cells have attempts=0 -> they came from finalize retire-unreached (finalize.py:454-460), not the reclaim cap. The cap is not doing the in-run termination its docstring claims for these runs.

Stuck-detection is last_progress-based (STUCK_WINDOW_S=1200) but a periodic resolve pass bumps last_progress independent of the lease, so all 1654 limbo cells read <5min 'fresh' and are never flagged, while the lease-based claim gate re-hands them.

defects.title: last_progress and lease_expires_at are two disagreeing clocks -> stuck-detection blind to lease-limbo reclaim thrash
defects.mechanism: claim_cells stamps both last_progress and lease_expires_at; resolve_cells (fired every SYNC_INTERVAL_S=120 by LIVE_CONVERGENCE) bumps last_progress on every matched cell but never the lease. A cell claimed >30min ago (lease expired -> re-claimable) still reads last_progress<5min, so the last_progress-based stuck-detector (STUCK_WINDOW_S=1200) never preempts it while the lease-based claim gate keeps re-handing it. Live: 1654/1703 testing cells in exactly this state.
defects.module_flag: ledger/service.py claim_cells:1393-1417 vs resolve_cells:1028; father stuck-detection STUCK_WINDOW_S. Fix would be flag-gated default-OFF (e.g. tie stuck-detection to lease_expires_at, or a scanner_ledger_progress_extends_lease knob).
defects.blast_radius: Coverage stalls: capacity re-claims warm-but-stale cells instead of untested ones; masks genuine hangs.

defects.title: 'attempted' terminal state conflates reclaim-exhaustion with never-reached starvation -> honest-coverage and thrash metrics are muddled
defects.mechanism: Two code paths write state='attempted': (a) release/reclaim when attempts>=cap (real exhaustion), (b) finalize.py:454-460 retire-unreached (scanner_finalize_retire_unreached=True) sweeping any applicable untested/empty-testing cell at scan end. In finalized scans (b) dominates (81%/55% of 'attempted' have attempts=0). A reader counting 'attempted' as 'thrashed to death' overstates thrash and hides that 22-39% of the surface was never tested.
defects.module_flag: finalize.py:454-460 (scanner_finalize_retire_unreached, default True) + ledger release/reclaim cap absorption. Distinguish with a separate na_reason/state (e.g. 'unreached' vs 'attempted') behind a default-OFF flag; report.py coverage already treats attempted as not-resolved.
defects.blast_radius: Buyer-visible coverage %: a scan that reached completed can have 22-39% of applicable cells never probed, reported only as 'attempted'.

defects.title: Capacity concentration: fleet re-claims a ~600-720 cell subset up to 6x while a comparable subset is never claimed once
defects.mechanism: claim_cells orders by vuln_class priority then updated_at then cell_id and re-hands expired-lease cells (which keep getting updated_at/last_progress bumped) ahead of never-touched cells that share priority. Net: the same subset is reclaimed repeatedly (attempts 2-6) while low-priority-class cells starve to finalize retire-unreached.
defects.module_flag: ledger/service.py claim_cells ORDER BY :1403 (array_position(ranked) NULLS LAST, updated_at, cell_id). A default-OFF 'prefer attempts=0 within a priority tier' tiebreak (ORDER BY ... , attempts ASC, updated_at) would spread capacity to unreached cells without changing class priority.
defects.blast_radius: 22-39% unreached surface per scan; reclaim effort has diminishing returns (35-48% of reclaimed cells still never converge).

role: WS-2 — OOB honest-classification + model-driver forensics (systems-architect, read-only)
summary: PART 1 (OOB honest-classification): The honest classifier FIRES exactly as designed in all three scans examined (prior nemotron 68a58881, prior bunny/OpenRouter infinity 1f5fe7c8, and the LIVE scan 84aea81a). classify_oob (service.py:77-97) derives the finding class from the callback PROTOCOL/beacon-provable label, never the agent's claim; sink-cluster (service.py:226-233, 279-292) collapses many callbacks per (host, honest_class) into one capped finding. Across the three scans the agent registered thousands of INFLATED OOB claims (cmdi, sqli, ssti, deserialization, lfi, rfi, nosqli, control, email_injection) yet ONLY ssrf and xxe were ever minted — every inflated/garbage claim that actually fired a scoped callback was downgraded to ssrf. The LIVE scan is the clearest proof: 17 callbacks the agent labeled `cmdi` (would-be CRITICAL RCE) were downgraded to ssrf and clustered into a single finding. The historical mass "confirmed via OOB" false-positive bug (one interaction → dozens of phantom cmdi/sqli/xss confirmations) is NOT present in any scan. Foreign-token and stale callbacks are correctly left unlinked. The jndi (ldap/rmi) path was not exercised (only empty-identity ldap connection-noise appeared, dropped at parse). PART 2 (model-driver forensics): WS-1's "~1082 model HTTP errors" is REFUTED as a large UNDERcount for nemotron and the "100% max_turns_exceeded" is CORROBORATED for the bunny route. Ground truth proxy_log.db (24,630 calls, ~24h, 100% nvidia/nemotron) shows 6,492 non-200 responses = 26.4% error rate (429×3578, 500×2834, client timeout/connect×49, 502×19, 504×12). agent.log surfaces only 13 of these (SDK retries mask the rest) plus 511 "Max turns (12) exceeded" verification failures that are actually just 10 distinct findings retried ~51× each — a retry-amplification, not 511 distinct HTTP errors. The OpenRouter/bunny blind spot is CONFIRMED: proxy_log.db logged zero non-nemotron traffic, and the infinity(bunny) workdir has no logs/agent.log at all, so its only failure signal is decisions.log — where 133/135 (98.5%) of entries are max_turns_exceeded, all tagged bunny.
current_state: classify_oob(reg_class, protocol) [CODE service.py:77-97]: ldap/ldaps/rmi protocol -> 'jndi'; otherwise strip _QUALIFIERS from the agent's claim label and keep it ONLY if every remaining token maps to the SAME beacon-provable class in _DIRECT={ssrf,xxe} (service.py:74); any other/combined/garbage label (cmdi/sqli/rce/ssti/xss/nosqli/...) -> downgraded to 'ssrf' with an '(agent suspected <claim>)' note. The callback proves an outbound fetch, not the bug class.

Sink-cluster + cap [CODE service.py:226-233 pre-pass, 279-292 mint gate]: one auto-minted finding per (scan_id, target_host, honest_class); _MINTED_SINKS dedup; ceiling _oob_finding_cap() default 12, env SCANNER_OOB_MAX_FINDINGS [CODE service.py:100-106]. Every endpoint that reached the same sink is folded into one finding's sink_endpoints list, not fanned into rows.

Scan-scoping gate [CODE registry.py:140-200 correlate/_scan_scoped]: a callback confirms only when it carries a real interactsh identity (unique-id/full-id) AND, when a registration floor is supplied from oob_health.json checked_at, its timestamp is >= that floor; otherwise the Match is returned unlinked (evidenced, never a finding). parse_interactions [registry.py:72-85] drops any record missing both id and host — this silently discards ldap connection-log noise with empty identity.

Minted finding shape [CODE service.py:440-516 _upsert_oob_finding]: title 'Blind <honest_class> confirmed via OOB callback'; evidence_paths records vuln_class_claimed vs vuln_class_confirmed so a downgrade is transparent; severity from honest class [service.py:36-56], so a downgraded cmdi lands as ssrf=high, never critical.

Model driver telemetry: an OpenAI-compatible proxy (proxy.py) logs every nemotron call to proxy_log.db table `calls` (status/error/tokens) [QUERY schema]; the in-container agent.log records only errors that survive SDK retry and surface via verification.failed. Non-nemotron (bunny/OpenRouter) routes are not fronted by this proxy and, for the infinity scan, no agent.log was persisted to the workdir root at all.
